Shit, man, you're lucky I found this. Next time you have this sort of question you should post to /v/fitness or /v/bodyweightfitness, that way I or someone else knowledgable on the subject will find it faster.

Your elbows should stay tucked into your body, your back and neck should stay straight, your shoulderblades should retract as you lower yourself. You should not lean any further forward or back as you go up and down. Your hands should be at different widths depending upon your strength level. They become harder as your place your hands closer together, so you should work towards diamond pushups to progress. Once you can easily do those you should progress to harder variations. This is all laid out in the /v/bodyweightfitness beginner routine.

Also, you should allow your chest to touch the floor at the bottom, but you should not bounce off of it. Lowering should be slow and controlled, and raising should be as fast as possible to generate maximum force. And having your elbows bend out isn't really good for anything besides hurting your joints. Not recommended.
